text_blocks.snippet: State and local agencies warn residents across Illinois to watch out for prevalent text, toll, and government impersonation scams.

list.snippet: DMV and Toll Text Scams: Scammers send fake text messages pretending to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or transit authorities. These messages claim you owe money for unpaid tolls or traffic tickets and threaten immediate license suspension. The state only texts for DMV appointment reminders.

Imposter Government Websites: Fraudulent websites mimic official state services (like vehicle registration renewals) to charge hidden fees and steal personal data. Always verify you are using official state portals like ilsos.gov .
Summer Travel and Rental Cons: Fake vacation rentals and misleading travel packages target travelers with vague descriptions and untraceable payment demands.
Debt Collection and Posing as Law Enforcement: Scammers call residents aggressively demanding immediate payment for fake debts using wire transfers, gift cards, or cryptocurrency.
Do Not Click Links: Ignore unsolicited text messages or emails claiming to come from state agencies or IDOT.
Verify Independently: If you receive a suspicious alert, navigate directly to official government websites rather than using links provided in messages.
Report Fraud : Report suspected text or online scams to the Federal Trade Commission or the Internet Crime Complaint Center .
